prompted_by: A conflict inside pass one, found while implementing it: the first R2 (rates re-learned at annual refits) missed P1-1's acceptance number, -0.0544 against -0.0582. Re-learning at every forecast date reproduced the review (-0.0582, 90% [-0.0961, -0.0261]), but P1-3's check that B1 at one regime reproduce R2 bit for bit needs the annual, aligned-month estimator.

decisions.decision: Option (B), amended so the end-to-end pin is not lost. (1) R2, the reference column, is the review's forecaster: the two rates are re-estimated at EVERY forecast date from condition-months published by that date and on or after the panel's first month. P1-1's acceptance is met: -0.0582, 90% [-0.0961, -0.0261], 98.33% [-0.1119, -0.0089]; record those as the pinned numbers. (2) The R2 estimator takes one explicit parameter, estimation cadence in {every forecast date, refit}, a function argument and never a RunSettings field; the column stores the first; the second exists only for the checks below and is computed on demand, not stored as a second column. (3) B1's required checks, restated before 0008 registers: (a) the committed function-level identity -- at one regime, B1's joint composition equals the chain composition on the same rates, bit for bit; and (b) an end-to-end identity on the real backtest frame -- B1 run with the state count fixed at one (the A2 mechanism, via state_count_for_the_backtest) writes a forecasts frame that equals, bit for bit by array equality, the R2 estimator at refit cadence applied over the same rows; this run is a pre-registered diagnostic, produces its frame with `forecast backtest` and is compared frame to frame, not through check-gates or `baseline compare`, so the regimes-exist gate and the zeros trap do not touch it. (4) B1's registration adds two pre-registered secondaries from that same diagnostic run: the cadence effect, R2 at refit cadence minus R2 at every forecast date, paired, one year, expected about -0.004 on this sample; and the pure regime effect, B1's scored run minus B1 at one regime, paired. Neither is an endpoint; 0008's primary for B1 stays B1 minus reference-0008. (5) Under 0007 every 'regimes help' reading is against monthly R2 and includes the cadence effect; that is charged to the model, because annual re-estimation of its rates is the model's own design and a reference should be as strong as it honestly can be.
decisions.reason: A null weaker than the cheapest honest forecaster flatters the model, which is the defect the review found and 0007 exists to remove; (A) would build that defect back in by choice. (B) keeps the strongest reference and the acceptance check keeps its purpose, proving the code is the review's forecaster. What (B) alone gives up is the end-to-end pin that B1 at one regime IS the chain on the real data; parameterising the estimator's cadence restores that pin as a diagnostic at the cost of a function argument, and the same run yields the decomposition that separates regime from cadence, so the confound the coordinator names becomes a reported number instead of a caveat. Neither cadence leaks: both count conditions published by the date used.
decisions.expects: The end-to-end identity holds bit for bit on the first attempt; the cadence effect measures between -0.003 and -0.005 at one year; B1's regimes-help reading is not decided by the cadence term.

wording_changes.0007: Replace the R2 definition in P1-2 with: 'R2, the condition chain -- per indicator, a two-state Markov chain on the monthly condition with two rates (entry hazard, persistence) estimated by plain counts from condition-months published by the forecast date and on or after the observation matrix's first month, re-estimated at every forecast date, started from the last published condition, stepping the publication gap and then the horizon. Pinned on the default fec79a040f9ca6f9 at one year: default minus R2 = -0.0582, 90% [-0.0961, -0.0261], 98.33% [-0.1119, -0.0089]; R1 one-year +0.1786, five +0.0690, ten -0.2109.' Add under 'regimes help': 'R2 is re-estimated monthly while the method's per-regime rates are re-estimated at annual refits; the comparison therefore includes that cadence difference, about -0.004 at one year on this sample, and it is charged to the method.'
wording_changes.0008: B1's required check becomes the two identities in P1-11 (3a, 3b), with the one-regime diagnostic run and its two secondaries (cadence effect; pure regime effect) named in the registration as measurements, not endpoints. B3's partner is the R2 column (monthly). The prerequisite list in P1-3 gains: 'the R2 estimator exposes its cadence as a function argument, with a test that the refit-cadence variant equals the model's one-regime rates on the aligned months.' The control arm's zero-difference requirement and reference-0008 are unchanged: R2 is a column and moves no forecast.

cautions: The cadence parameter is a function argument, never a RunSettings field; a field would change the configuration hash and the fit-cache key.

The one-regime B1 run is a diagnostic frame, not a scored arm: do not route it through check-gates (regimes-exist fails at one state by construction) or through `baseline compare` (the zeros trap); compare frames by array equality.
If the end-to-end identity (3b) fails, that is a defect in B1 or in the R2 estimator and is investigated before B1's scored run; the identity is not loosened to a tolerance.
Do not re-estimate the model's own per-regime rates monthly to remove the cadence term; that would change the default and move reference-0008 under the slate.
executor_notes: 3b as literally worded cannot hold on any-time rows: B1 leaves the any-time path unchanged and that path does not step the publication gap, so its rows cannot equal the gap-stepping chain by construction. 0008 registers 3b on the point-in-time rows B1 changes, and requires any-time rows at one regime to equal the model's own unchanged any-time composition. Stated before the run.

P1-3(ii)'s refusal in `forecast baseline compare` is implemented as the flag --require-own-artifacts, always passed by scripts/research_arm.sh, rather than as the default: the existing test contract deliberately reads a comparison under evaluation settings (resamples, seed) that differ from the producing run's, and an unconditional refusal would forbid that. The harness also makes no comparison at all when check-gates fails. Together these close the trap for every arm.

P1-6(3) asked that evaluation/verdict.py take the pre-registration path from its caller. It instead derives the path from the module's own location, which removes the upward import the layer check flags without changing the fourteen call sites (notebook 03, the tests, a research derivation) that rely on the default.

P1-3 cites a '+0.0295 threshold' in experiment 0006. 0006's registration contains no such number; its only bar is the one-year 90% interval lying entirely above zero. The 0006 amendment says so and adds nothing.
